dpa.structure: Independent public authority run as a collegial body: a President and six members, each with an alternate, serving a single non-renewable six-year term (Art. 11 Law 4624/2019).
dpa.regional: Single national authority, no regional DPAs.

law.name: Law 4624/2019 (Government Gazette A 137/29.08.2019), implementing the GDPR and transposing Directive 2016/680

complaint.how: Through the HDPA online portal using Taxisnet credentials; those without access can email a complaint form (in English if the infringement occurred in Greece) to complaints@dpa.gr. No fee identified.
complaint.contact_controller_first: Yes: the HDPA states that complainants must first address the controller, and may decline to examine a complaint if this was not done.
complaint.deadlines: No time limit for complaining and no fixed decision deadline confirmed; the HDPA must inform the complainant of progress and outcome within a reasonable period (Art. 13 Law 4624/2019).
complaint.complainant_status: not confirmed (the HDPA cannot award compensation; that requires a civil court).

stages: Complaint via portal, checked for prior exercise of rights with the controller
Investigation or audit by Authority members or authorised staff (Art. 15(2))
Prior hearing of the persons concerned before any adverse measure (Art. 15)
Decision with warnings, compliance orders, processing limits or bans and/or Art. 83 fines (Art. 15)
procedure.decision_maker: The Authority as a collegial body (President and members); whether a given case is decided in plenary or in a chamber was not confirmed.

fines.imposed_by: The HDPA itself, by administrative decision.
fines.public_bodies: Yes: public sector bodies can be fined up to EUR 10 million (Art. 39 Law 4624/2019).
fines.quirks: Criminal offences in Art. 38 Law 4624/2019, with prison terms up to 10 years for the most serious unauthorised access or disclosure cases.

appeal.court: Action for annulment (αίτηση ακύρωσης) before the Council of State (Συμβούλιο της Επικρατείας), the supreme administrative court, against HDPA regulatory and individual acts (Art. 20 Law 4624/2019).
appeal.deadline: not confirmed in Law 4624/2019 (believed to follow the general 60-day Council of State rule, not verified for this packet).
appeal.suspensive: No: the time limit for, and filing of, an annulment action does not suspend the decision (Art. 20). A separate request for suspension is believed possible but was not confirmed.
appeal.further: None: the Council of State is first and last instance.

private.courts: Civil courts where the controller or processor is established or where the data subject habitually resides (Art. 40 Law 4624/2019).
private.collective: Data subjects may mandate a not-for-profit body to lodge complaints on their behalf (Art. 41 Law 4624/2019). Court representation and Representative Actions Directive transposition coverage not confirmed.

cases.title: Ministry of Finance v HDPA (taxpayer data breach)
cases.summary: The HDPA fined the General Secretariat of Information Systems EUR 150,000 for inadequate security after a breach affecting nearly all taxpayers (decisions 98/2013 and 117/2014). The Council of State (decision 339/2019) dismissed the Minister's annulment action.

cases.title: Cosmote / OTE (2020 data breach)
cases.summary: HDPA fines totalling EUR 9.25 million (January 2022) after a breach affecting over 10 million subscribers. The companies brought annulment actions at the Council of State, heard in May 2023; outcome not confirmed.

quirks: Direct one-step judicial review: HDPA decisions go straight to the Council of State, with no lower court and no further appeal.
Public bodies can be fined, capped at EUR 10 million (Art. 39).
Complaints are filed through a Taxisnet-authenticated portal, and prior contact with the controller is expected.
Pre-GDPR, fines on public bodies were already upheld by the Council of State (339/2019).
plain: You first ask the organisation to fix the problem, then complain to the HDPA through its online portal. The seven-member Authority investigates, hears the organisation and can order changes or impose a fine. The organisation can ask the Council of State to annul the decision, but that does not pause it, and compensation has to be claimed separately in the civil courts.
confidence: Medium: structure, fines and court route are confirmed from the HDPA's translation of Law 4624/2019; I could not confirm the annulment deadline, the limitation period, complainant party status, or the outcome of the OTE/Cosmote appeal.
